description: Export spec for birch tree with 3 LOD levels

visual_traits.bark: White/cream with dark horizontal lenticels (birch marks)
visual_traits.silhouette: Tall and slender, often with slight lean

LOD0.name: birch_0
LOD0.notes: Full detail - visible bark texture, individual leaf cards

LOD1.name: birch_0_lod1
LOD1.notes: Mid-range - simplified bark, merged leaf clusters

LOD2.name: birch_0_lod2
LOD2.notes: Far distance - cylinder trunk + simple cone/sphere canopy, or engine uses procedural

uv_convention.description: Engine shader uses UV.y to distinguish bark from canopy for procedural fallback

trunk.notes: All trunk/bark vertices must have UV.y between 0.0 and 1.0

canopy.notes: All leaf/canopy vertices must have UV.y greater than 1.0

uv_convention.enforcement: If UV.y > 1.0, shader renders green (canopy). If UV.y <= 1.0, shader renders brown (bark).

texture.notes: White/cream base with dark horizontal marks
Leaf atlas with alpha cutout, bright green

all_lods: Origin at trunk base center (Y=0 at ground)
Verify UV convention: bark UV.y < 1.0, leaves UV.y > 1.0
LOD0: Keep detail on bark texture UVs
LOD2: Or skip and let engine use procedural LOD

lod_creation: 2. Duplicate, apply Decimate modifier (ratio ~0.15) for LOD1
3. For LOD2: Create simple cylinder+cone primitive OR skip
4. Verify UVs survived decimation (check UV editor)
5. Export each LOD to separate GLB files

engine_integration.notes: LOD2 can be skipped - engine generates procedural LOD1 if _lod1 mesh not found
